correctness.rationale: After normalizing one singleton to 0, let A label the n-part and z the other singleton. The exact induced-difference criterion makes A-A disjoint from -A and z-A, while (-A)∩(z-A) would force z into the nonedge difference set A-A. Since |A-A|>=n and the two translates each have size n, every host has order at least 3n. The explicit Cayley graph on Z_3×Z_n with connection set consisting of nonzero first coordinates contains K_{1,1,n} induced, giving equality. All quantifiers and the n>=2 boundary were checked. The bundled verifier exhaustively excludes smaller finite abelian hosts for n=2..5 and checks the construction through n=50; finite checks are not used as the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The closest primary source explicitly leaves the relevant unbalanced complete-multipartite eta problem open and highlights K_{1,1,5} with bounds 10 and 15. The new lower bound is statement-level stronger than its local floor: it forces three pairwise disjoint difference sets and proves 3n for the whole K_{1,1,n} family. The older complete-multipartite representation-number theory is a stricter cyclic/unitary-host invariant and does not imply eta=3n. Focused semantic searches found no covering exact statement; residual alias risk is retained.

value.rationale: This is a natural exact subproblem singled out by the initiating eta paper, not an arbitrary parameter slice: K_{1,1,5} is explicitly presented there as a concrete unresolved gap, and the paper calls unbalanced complete multipartite graphs a broader open direction. The result closes that example and the entire K_{1,1,n} family with a reusable multi-neighborhood difference-set obstruction, showing the published local floor 2n can be off by a factor 3/2 on this family.
